{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q010_rossmann_family_function_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, these are three distinct families within the same NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold superfamily, c.2.1 (sunid 51735): alcohol dehydrogenase-like C-terminal domains, c.2.1.1 (51736); CoA-binding domains, c.2.1.8 (51900); and potassium-channel NAD-binding domains, c.2.1.9 (63944). They also share fold c.2 (51734) and class c, Alpha and beta proteins (51349).

The shared superfamily expresses SCOPe’s inference of probable common ancestry despite potentially weak sequence similarity. Separate families distinguish more closely related groups within that broader evolutionary relationship. Fold membership alone establishes similar structural architecture, not necessarily homology; class membership describes secondary-structure organization and is weaker still.

Biologically, this illustrates divergence of a Rossmann scaffold into different functional contexts: nicotinamide-cofactor binding in alcohol-dehydrogenase-like proteins, CoA binding in proteins such as succinyl-CoA synthetase, and channel-associated regulatory domains. The superfamily’s NAD(P)-binding name does not establish NAD(P) binding or oxidoreductase activity for every member. Likewise, the potassium-channel family name does not prove that every member binds NAD or that the classified domain forms the ion-conducting pore.

Do not transfer alcohol-dehydrogenase activity, CoA specificity, NAD versus NADP preference, catalytic residues, or channel regulation between these families solely from classification. This relationship concerns domains, not necessarily entire proteins. Specific functional assignments require sequence/profile evidence, conserved binding and catalytic residues in structural context, ligand-bound structures or binding measurements, biochemical activity assays, and—where relevant—channel electrophysiology. These are needed validation types, not evidence obtained here. A cross-family structure may help model the conserved core, but cannot automatically template substrate-binding loops, active sites, interfaces, or whole-protein architecture. Prefer a well-aligned, experimentally characterized representative from the target family; no single representative captures all three families’ functions.","evidence_used":["Pretrained model knowledge","/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=alcohol","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51736","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51735","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=CoA-binding","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=potassium","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51734","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=CoA","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/63944","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51349","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/c.2.1.5","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=CoA&limit=200","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51900"]}]}
